steps.what: Assess client requirements and the design properties and condition of available floral materials
Plan the arrangement or select an appropriate standard design pattern

tasks.design: Keep arrangement planning human, using existing pattern references in {DOCS} where useful. The designer checks actual materials and chooses a design that fits the client's needs and the properties of the flowers.
tasks.previous_blocker: A plausible picture does not establish that available flowers will create a suitable physical arrangement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native reference records can support standard pattern selection; no new image generation is needed for the task.
tasks.still_hard: Freshness, structure, colour and the intended occasion require direct observation and aesthetic judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The designer adapts the idea to the real materials and the client's intention.
tasks.altitude: Design time and creative responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Choose materials that realise an intended visual effect

evidence.claim: Floral planning depends on actual material properties and aesthetic judgement; generated concepts alone do not complete the task.

assumptions: Boundary is planning or selecting an arrangement design, excluding the separately owned client conversation, flower preparation, assembly and delivery. The client conversation produces its brief before this task begins and is counted once.

Client and designer produce the arrangement brief through their existing conversation; supplier delivery and stock handling produce the available materials through unchanged work. Designer checks the brief and materials in s1 and records the plan in s2, with all time retained.
No free structured flower condition, suitability or design-choice flag is assumed. Keep native references and current practice; no new system or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: How frequently standard designs fit actual client needs
How variable material availability and condition are
research_questions: Can the chosen plan be made from the actual materials while meeting the client's stated intention?

already_counted.description: Assess materials and plan or select the arrangement design

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Material assessment and design retain full time; no image-generation runtime is treated as completed floral design.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree client arrangement and delivery needs

steps.what: Confer with clients about price, arrangement type and delivery date, time and place

tasks.design: Keep the client conversation human and record the agreed brief in {DOCS}. The designer clarifies the occasion, acceptable price and delivery details with the client instead of treating an intake form as the conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clients may not initially know which arrangement will express what they want.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native brief records support the discussion; no additional automation is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Budget, emotional intent and practical delivery constraints can require negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: The designer hears the client's intention and helps turn it into a realistic request.
tasks.altitude: Client discussion and agreement responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify client intent and practical constraints

evidence.claim: Agreeing a floral arrangement and delivery combines personal communication and practical judgement; no labour saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is the conversation and recording its agreement, excluding designing and making the arrangement, delivery execution and taking payment. Resolve shared brief capture once across tasks.

Client produces wishes and delivery details during this conversation. Designer elicits, verifies and records type, price agreement, delivery date, time, address and contact details within the retained 100 hours; no free structured address or preference record is assumed.

Existing shop price guidance and delivery availability come from normal operations and are checked during the conversation. Unclear requirements return to direct clarification, not automatic acceptance.
Keep current native brief records. No new form, model or process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Which clients require additional help describing an arrangement
research_questions: Can the client and designer repeat the same agreed price, arrangement expectation and delivery details?

already_counted.description: Clarify wishes and verify and capture the complete arrangement and delivery agreement

incremental.description: No changed process or new upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Conversation and brief capture retain full effort; no client or delivery time is counted as focal saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Serve retail customers and keep financial records

steps.what: Serve customers, answer telephones and sell giftware items
Receive payment and capture the sale and tender details in the retail till
Copy recorded sales and payment amounts into parallel financial record lists
Check financial records, reconcile payment exceptions and accept the shop record

tasks.design: Use the transaction record in {OTHER}, the retail point-of-sale system, as the shop's source record and replace a duplicate {SPREADSHEET} list with a native view or export. Customer service, payment capture and financial reconciliation remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some shops re-enter the same recorded sales for office record keeping.
tasks.enabler_now: Native transaction views can provide the existing record without a second manually maintained list.
tasks.still_hard: Payment exceptions, cash differences and customer questions still need direct attention.
tasks.human_edge: The designer serves the customer and recognises when a financial record does not match the real transaction.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate sales copying where it exists; service and reconciliation duties stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Source records and simple transaction reconciliation

evidence.claim: Using an existing point-of-sale transaction view can remove duplicate manual sales lists where such lists exist; the proposed hours are unmeasured model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is retail service, payment receipt and shop-level financial records, excluding client design consultation, arrangement pricing and external bookkeeping. A shop already using one source record has no s3 saving.

Floral designer produces transaction identifier, timestamp, sold item, quantity, unit price, total, currency, tender type and payment reference during s2's retained 25 hours. The native view replacing s3 consumes this existing record; no free structured sale capture is assumed.

Customers supply payment during s2; payment providers or normal cash handling produce settlement records after the transaction and before its s4 reconciliation. No new provider work is introduced. Additional bookkeeping configuration upkeep is counted below.

Missing references, refunds or mismatched payments remain manually reconciled in s4's 15 hours. Try native views before custom integration; no automatic acceptance of financial completeness or new payment authority is proposed.
unknowns: Whether parallel manual sales lists actually exist
Whether native views satisfy the shop's record needs
research_questions: Can the shop reconcile sampled sales and settlements without maintaining a duplicate list?

already_counted.description: Serve customers, capture transactions and reconcile records including exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain native sales views and check record links

approvals.approved_version: Exact shop record period, transaction snapshot, settlement references and unresolved exception list; edits void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85, gross=15; subtract 5 focal upkeep for central net=10. Range assumes only part of duplicate copying is removable. One other-role upkeep hour is outside focal savings; service, payment capture and reconciliation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Wrap completed arrangements to protect and present the flowers
Price the completed arrangement and attach the correct price indication

tasks.design: Keep physical wrapping and arrangement pricing human, using the shop's existing price guidance in {DOCS} where required. The designer checks the actual arrangement and attaches its price indication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protection, presentation and pricing depend on the completed physical arrangement.
tasks.enabler_now: Current wrapping materials and native price references already support the task.
tasks.still_hard: Individual arrangements differ in condition, materials and presentation needs.
tasks.human_edge: The designer handles fragile materials and judges an appropriate finished presentation.
tasks.altitude: Wrapping and pricing effort remain unchanged.

reach.task: Protect and present finished decorative work

evidence.claim: Wrapping is physical handling and arrangement pricing needs the actual item and current guidance; no labour saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is wrapping and pricing the completed arrangement, excluding designing, assembling, payment receipt and delivery. Arrangement completion is produced by the separately owned making task before s1.

Designer observes the actual arrangement and produces its wrapping in s1, then verifies materials and captures the price indication within s2's retained time. Existing shop management supplies price guidance; no free structured bill of materials or price flag is assumed.
Keep current native references and wrapping practice. No new system, capture requirement or process means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: How standard versus bespoke arrangement prices are set
Which wrapping requirements vary with delivery or occasion
research_questions: Does the finished wrapping protect the arrangement and display the intended price clearly?

already_counted.description: Wrap the arrangement, determine its price and attach the indication

incremental.description: No new wrapping or pricing process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Physical wrapping and item-specific pricing keep full time; no unobserved structured material data or hardware automation is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: A shop with duplicate sales records may reduce copying, while client discussion, floral judgement and physical finishing retain full time.
reach: Explore material presentation with set and exhibit designers
Learn client needs discovery from commercial and industrial designers
skills_to_grow: Keep clear client and delivery agreements
Check the actual condition and properties of floral materials
Reconcile source transaction records without duplicate lists
role.ambitious_version: Provide thoughtful floral work and dependable client service with simple, traceable retail records.
